subject: radiation-therapy
intro: Radiation therapy leads into the radiation oncology team — the therapists on the treatment machine, the dosimetrists who plan the dose, and the imaging and nuclear-medicine technologists who share the physics.

roles.title: Radiation Therapists
roles.what: Deliver radiation therapy to patients as prescribed by a radiation oncologist: review the prescription, prepare immobilisation and protection devices, operate the linac and support patients through treatment.
roles.where: Units 1 and 2 are the daily craft — linear accelerator operation, dose calculation, simulation and immobilisation, target volumes and organs at risk — with unit 3's side-effect management shaping patient care.

roles.title: Medical Dosimetrists
roles.what: Generate radiation treatment plans and dose calculations, work out how to cover the tumour while sparing healthy tissue, and supervise and consult on how the plan is delivered.
roles.where: Unit 2's target volumes, organs at risk and 3D and IMRT planning is the job itself, and unit 6's machine QA and radiation safety underpin the plan's sign-off.

roles.title: Radiologic Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Take x-rays and CAT scans and administer nonradioactive materials for diagnostic imaging, positioning patients and producing the images physicians use to diagnose and stage disease.
roles.where: Unit 1's radiation physics and beam characteristics and unit 2's simulation work share the imaging foundation, and unit 3's patient care covers the positioning and consent work imaging demands.

roles.title: Nuclear Medicine Technologists
roles.what: Prepare and administer radioactive isotopes for diagnostic and therapeutic studies, calculate doses and operate radioisotope equipment to image organ function.
roles.where: Unit 1's dose calculation fundamentals and beam characteristics and unit 6's radiation safety in therapy are the shared physics, extended by unit 5's brachytherapy isotope handling.
